rsm:PollutantRelease.rsm:RemarkText:
Operator believes that this is due to the emissions from the kiln being on bypass due to the breakdown of the flue gas scrubber.
As reported to Barnsley MBC, the operator became aware of problems with the flue gas scrubber which after being emptied (£10,000) and an investigation undertaken of the inside of the scrubber unit, brought about the decision to replace the scrubber unit with a similar replacement unit. It was deemed that the damaged unit was beyond economic and safe repair and that the purchase and installation of a replacement unit their only option, but that this would take some time.
From the time the investigations started on the old scrubber unit to the commissioning of the replacement unit, the kiln emissions are on bypass and as such no ‘scrubbing effect’ can take place.
The replacement unit is due to be built during December 2016 and commissioned early January 2017. The cost of the project is circa £250,000.
Operator fully expects the new unit to bring emission levels down to permitted levels.
